FCCPS AI Advisory Committee Chair Sync

Sun, Mar 08, 2026 7:30PM • 35:03

**SUMMARY KEYWORDS**

AI Advisory Committee, policy recommendations, consensus, dissenting views, grade bands, student use, implementation, public opinion, school board, meeting structure, action items, stakeholder feedback, resource allocation, committee roles, AI skepticism.

John Black expressed concerns about the AI Advisory Committee's lack of progress and consensus on policy recommendations. Two members, Tom Colvin and David Berol, are particularly opposed to AI and have blocked progress. Bethany Henderson suggested focusing on majority opinions and capturing dissenting views for the school board. Tina Beaty proposed level-setting and discussing AI's application across different grade bands. John Black emphasized the need for substantive recommendations despite differing opinions. The committee was advised to prepare written submissions before the next meeting to streamline discussion. Bethany and Jerrod will send a re-leveling email to guide the committee's next steps.

-   [REDACTED] Black - Distribute the minutes from the last meeting and publish a rough draft on the Miro board so members can review materials and start drafting inputs before the next meeting
-   [REDACTED] Black - Have a one-on-one conversation with the committee member who is uncomfortable with the use of AI to clarify human-in-the-loop processes, address concerns, and attempt to bring them along before the next meeting
-   Co-send the re-leveling email to the committee (partnering with Bethany) to set expectations for the next meeting and request written inputs from members
-   Send a re-leveling email to the committee that clarifies the committee's purpose, expectations for the next meeting, and guidance on submitting written comments; include context that dissenting views will be captured and that members should prepare written inputs before the next meeting
-   Coordinate and schedule a short prep call (email to propose times) between Tina and John toward the end of the week to prepare for the next Friday meeting

heading_path: Concerns About Meeting Productivity and Consensus
sections.text:
-   John Black expresses concerns about the committee's productivity and the lack of consensus on key issues.
-   Bethany Henderson suggests that the committee's goal is not to write the policy but to provide parameters and considerations for the school board.
-   John Black mentions that two committee members, Tom Coleman and David, are particularly opposed to AI and have been blocking progress.
-   Bethany Henderson advises focusing on the majority's opinions and capturing dissenting views for the school board.

heading_path: Differences in Opinions and Process Concerns
sections.text:
-   Tina Beaty inquires about the specific issues that Tom and David have with the process and AI.
-   John Black explains that Tom is generally hostile to AI, while David is more concerned with the process and implementation details.
-   The committee has been spending a lot of time on David's restrictive proposals, which have not gained broad support.
-   John Black suggests that the committee should clarify its role and focus on providing guidance rather than writing policy.

-   Tina Beaty proposes a level-setting exercise to clarify the committee's purpose and build from there.
-   John Black mentions that the committee has already identified some areas of agreement and disagreement.
-   Bethany Henderson suggests focusing on grade bands as a way to structure the discussion without getting bogged down in specifics.
-   John Black emphasizes that the committee should not try to define grade bands but use them as a framework for discussion.

-   Bethany Henderson recommends sending an email to the committee to re-level set and provide guidance for the next meeting.
-   John Black suggests that dissenting views should be captured and not ignored, but the committee should focus on moving forward.
-   Tina Beaty proposes using the next meeting to coalesce around key themes rather than sticking to a strict structure.
-   John Black agrees and mentions that the committee should aim for substantive progress rather than getting bogged down in details.

heading_path: Addressing Trust Issues and Personal Concerns
sections.text:
-   Bethany Henderson suggests having a one-on-one conversation with Tom to address his trust issues with AI and the process.
-   John Black explains that Tom believes corporate giants are conspiring to wipe out civilization, which complicates the discussion.
-   Bethany Henderson advises explaining the role of humans in the loop and setting guardrails to address Tom's concerns.
-   John Black agrees to have the conversation and see if it helps Tom participate more effectively.

-   John Black mentions that he will push out the minutes from the last meeting and have a rough draft ready for the next meeting.
-   Bethany Henderson and John Black discuss the importance of capturing dissenting views and not ignoring them.
-   Tina Beaty suggests connecting towards the end of the week to prepare for the next meeting.
-   John Black and Bethany Henderson thank everyone for their time and efforts, emphasizing the importance of the committee's work.
